input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator condition was inverted to `not any_prefix_is_slash`, so ordinary options are joined with "; " and slash-prefixed options with " / ", the reverse of the original behavior.
- rationale: Trigger: any option such as `--verbose` with `-v` and no slash prefix. The new expression evaluates to "; " because any_prefix_is_slash is False, so the help left column renders as `-v; --verbose` instead of `-v, --verbose`. This changes help output for nearly every option, which users and docs tests would observe.
critique: Both the finding and the label point to the same fault: the separator condition was inverted to `not any_prefix_is_slash`, so ordinary options get '; ' and slash-prefixed options get ' / '. The finding's specific example (`-v, --verbose` becoming `-v; --verbose`) may misdescribe which part of the help output changes. The underlying mechanism is still the same.
